key_insight: A scenario-free robust bilevel DLMP framework coordinates EV active/reactive charging and network dispatch to cut charging cost while improving voltage security under uncertain load and PV output.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical distribution-network control tool for utilities and EV aggregators by embedding uncertainty-aware pricing, voltage constraints, and reactive power support into one optimization stack.
method: Upper level: EV aggregator schedules active and reactive charging to minimize cost under DLMPs.
Lower level: network EMS solves constrained dispatch and computes DLMPs with feeder/voltage limits.
Uses a compact robust counterpart for normal-minus-beta net-demand uncertainty, then KKT + Big-M linearization to make the bilevel model tractable.
evidence_signal: On the IEEE 33-bus distribution system, the approach improved voltage security and reduced computational complexity compared with conventional stochastic and robust methods.
watch_item: The KKT/Big-M reformulation and DLMP exactness depend on modeling assumptions and careful calibration, so implementation may be sensitive to parameter choices.
paper_title: Scenario-Free Uncertainty-Aware DLMP-Based Bilevel Coordination of EV Charging and Reactive Power Support in Distribution Networks
